chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Yunus, who said:

I wrote to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'Fish that do not have scales, can they be eaten?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Among the fish, there are some that have spines/roughness, so they rub against everything, and their scales go away. But when its two ends differ, meaning its tail and its head, then eat it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for eating fish that lack scales according to Imam Al-Reza?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the criterion for permissible fish by distinguishing between scaleless varieties that rub off their scales and those with distinct heads and tails, a view that underpins the Shia juristic preference for the 'head and tail' sign over the 'scales' sign found in other schools. This narration highlights the practical application of distinguishing features (al-alamah) in dietary laws, emphasizing that the presence of separate head and tail is the definitive indicator of permissibility regardless of scale presence.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih Bin Al Sandy, from Yunus who said,

‘I wrote to Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The fish which does not happen to have scales on it, can I eat?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the fishes which happens to have evilness for it, so it attaches with everything, so its scales go away, but when its sides are different, meaning its tail and its head, so eat it’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Salih al-Sindiy from Yunus who has said the following:

“I once wrote to abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and asked if fish which has no scales can be used for food. He (the Imam) said, ‘Of fish there are those which have bad manners and they rub against everything and its scales go away, but if its two ends are different, its tail and head, then you can use it for food.’”
